name: aboard
description: VS Code integration for visible Claude Code and ChatGPT sessions, fleet tracking, and Auto Run orchestration.

viewsWelcome.contents:
aboard provides visible terminals for coding-agent sessions, fleet tracking, and Auto Run orchestration.

One click sets this workspace up: launch configuration, Auto Run setup, and a loopback-only bridge. The existing configuration is preserved.
[Initialize](command:aboard.initializeProject)

This project's aboard assets were created by another extension version. Update them before starting or resuming aboard. Files edited by the user are preserved and listed for review.
[Update .abd/](command:aboard.updateProject)
What aboard's agents and runs did most recently shows up here, including sessions the user can reopen.

commandPalette.when: aboard.initialized && (aboard.autoRunCard == recoverable || aboard.autoRunCard == broken || aboard.autoRunCard == unsupported)

aboard.bridge.port.description: Preferred loopback port. If occupied, aboard selects an ephemeral port.

aboard.launch.maxInlinePromptChars.description: Longest prompt passed inline as a command-line argument. Longer prompts spill to one-use files in the OS temporary directory and are referenced with @path.

aboard.terminals.closeOnSessionEnd.description: Close an agent's terminal when its session ends. Off by default: exiting the session and closing the terminal are separate gestures, so the terminal is left at a shell prompt for the user to reuse or close. The agent leaves the fleet either way, and relaunching it is never blocked by the leftover terminal.

aboard.autoRun.review.description: Launch an Auto Run reviewer after each issue is addressed.

aboard.autoRun.branchMode.description: Use one branch and pull request per issue, or commit all issues directly to the run session branch and use only its cumulative pull request.

aboard.autoRun.exploreBeforeImplement.description: Launch a visible read-only Explore agent immediately before each fresh auto-run implementer. Its bounded codebase report is passed directly to the implementer and published best-effort on the issue. The setting is frozen when a run starts and preserved across resume.

aboard.autoRun.issueContextDepth.description: How many relation levels of issue context an auto-run worker is given. 0 loads the run's own issue alone; 1 adds its direct parents, sub-issues, and same-repository references; each further level continues the traversal by one more hop. Bounded by at most 50 related issues, the newest 20 comments per issue, and roughly 60,000 characters. This changes loaded issue bodies only, not the worker's instructions.

aboard.autoRun.prompt.markdownDescription: Persistent note added near the end of every Auto Run implementer and reviewer prompt. It is inserted before the per-run note supplied after `/auto`, so that dynamic note remains last and can refine the configured guidance. The value is frozen when a run starts and preserved across resume.

aboard.autoRun.pauseAfterHitl.description: Pause before launching the next issue after a HITL acceptance commit has been published, reviewed if configured, and integrated. Resume Auto Run starts the next issue.

aboard.autoRun.mergeStrategy.description: How auto-run merges a pull request. Squash by default because one issue is one logical change even when the engine made two commits. A final run pull request carrying unpublished target commits is left open for squash or rebase until those commits are pushed; merge preserves their ancestry and remains safe.

aboard.autoRun.mergeRunPullRequest.description: Merge the run's own pull request when the run ends. An auto-run addresses each issue on its own branch, merges those into one session branch, and opens a single pull request from it into the branch active when the run started. Off by default: that branch is one the user is working on, so a conflict there is likely and landing a batch of automated work on it is the user's decision. When on, aboard attempts the merge once, reconciles a conflict it can resolve, and otherwise leaves the pull request open for the user.

enumDescriptions: Forget the run record only. Terminals, the checkout, branches, commits, pull requests, and issues are all left exactly as they are.
Also close the run's terminals, remove its own checkout when that checkout is clean, and delete its local branches when they still point where the run left them.
Local cleanup, plus close the run's still-open unmerged pull requests and delete its unmerged remote branches. Merged work, moved branches, and closed issues are never touched.
aboard.autoRun.discardBehavior.description: What Discard removes besides the run record. Cleanup never deletes a dirty checkout, an artifact whose SHA or pull request identity changed, or anything that already merged.

aboard.autoRun.worktree.enabled.description: Give an auto-run a checkout of its own instead of working in the user's files. The run creates a second checkout beside the project, carries ignored local .claude and .abd configuration into it without replacing tracked files, and leaves the user's working tree and branch exactly as they are. Off by default: a separate checkout costs a full copy of the tree plus whatever the session-setup script installs into it.

aboard.autoRun.worktree.root.description: Where a run's own checkout is created. Empty uses a sibling of the project directory. The path must be outside the project, or the run would address issues in a directory the repository itself contains.

aboard.autoRun.worktree.keep.description: Keep a run's own checkout after the run ends. Off by default, in which case aboard removes it once the queue drains; but always keeps it when the run stopped or parked an issue, because its terminals and unfinished work are in there.

aboard.autoRun.worktree.setupTimeoutSeco.description: How long .abd/session-setup.ps1 or .abd/session-setup.sh may take in a fresh checkout. Those files ship empty; put the user's installation steps in them (copying an .env, npm install, uv sync) and aboard runs the one for this platform once, right after creating the checkout. A failure refuses the run rather than starting agents in a half-installed tree.

scripts.test:integration: npm run test && npm run test:vscode
scripts.test:vscode: npm run build && npm run test:vscode:build && node dist/vscode-test/run.js
scripts.package: npm run check && npm run build -- --minify && npm run package:build && node dist/package.js
scripts.e2e:bootstrap: npm run e2e:build && node dist/e2e/cli.js bootstrap
scripts.e2e:reset: npm run e2e:build && node dist/e2e/cli.js reset
scripts.e2e:serve: npm run e2e:build && node dist/e2e/cli.js serve
scripts.e2e:smoke: npm run e2e:build && node dist/e2e/cli.js smoke
scripts.e2e:chatgpt: npm run e2e:build && node dist/e2e/cli.js chatgpt
scripts.e2e:extension: npm run build && npm run e2e:extension:build && node dist/e2e/vscode/run.js
scripts.e2e:auto-run: npm run build && npm run e2e:build && npm run e2e:extension:build && node dist/e2e/vscode/auto-run.js
scripts.e2e:full: npm run check && npm run test:integration && npm run build && npm run e2e:chatgpt && npm run e2e:reset && npm run e2e:reset && npm run e2e:smoke && npm run e2e:reset && npm run e2e:extension && npm run e2e:reset && npm run e2e:auto-run && npm run e2e:reset
